value: Anne Shirley came to live at Green Gables
unit: Anne Shirley came to live at Green Gables with Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert at the age of eleven. She attended school in Avonlea under Mr. Phillips and later Miss Stacy, forming a deep friendship with Diana Barry and entering a intense academic rivalry with Gilbert Blythe. She took part in local school concerts and formed the Avonlea Village Improvement Society as its secretary. After preparing in the Queen's class, she attended Queen's Academy to earn her teacher's license alongside her classmates. Following her studies, she chose to stay in Avonlea to teach local children and assist Marilla.

label: History
value: Anthony Pye is an orphan.
unit: Anthony Pye is an orphan who was taken in by his aunt, Mrs. George Pye, and enrolled in the Avonlea school under Anne Shirley. On his first day, he sat sullenly at a corner desk and later poured slate-bottle water down Aurelia Clay's neck, remaining completely untouched by Anne's lecture on being a gentleman. He openly voiced his dislike for Anne to other children, claiming female teachers were useless. In school, he habitually obeyed Anne with a scornful air of toleration and caused minor trouble, such as mocking her or planting a mouse in her desk drawer. After the mouse incident, Anne lost her temper and whipped him with a pointer, causing him to winced and cry, which left Anne feeling she had permanently lost any chance of winning his affection.

label: History
value: Charlotta came to live at Echo Lodge.
unit: Charlotta came to live at Echo Lodge to serve Miss Lavendar Lewis for board and clothes, following in the footsteps of her elder sisters Charlotta, Julietta, and Evelina. Because Miss Lavendar calls all the Bowman sisters "Charlotta" to avoid confusion, she became "Charlotta the Fourth." She welcomed Anne Shirley and Diana Barry warmly during their visits to Echo Lodge, bonding with them and practicing in front of a mirror to copy Anne's graceful movements and chin uplift. When Miss Lavendar became quiet and withdrawn, Charlotta grew deeply concerned for her well-being, especially when Miss Lavendar failed to scold her after she accidentally broke an heirloom bowl. She later assisted Anne in sewing a new organdy dress for Miss Lavendar and helped prepare Echo Lodge for Miss Lavendar's upcoming wedding.

label: History
value: Davy Keith and his twin sister Dora were orphaned.
unit: Davy Keith and his twin sister Dora were orphaned after their mother's long illness and were taken in as third cousins by Marilla Cuthbert at Green Gables. Arriving with very little upbringing, Davy immediately formed a deep affection for Anne Shirley while simultaneously developing a jealous resentment toward Paul Irving. Shortly after his arrival, Davy got into various misdeeds, such as lying, locking Dora in the shed, hanging over the well-box looking for where the dark goes, and stepping on lemon pies after climbing forbidden shelves. Marilla and Anne undertook to train and reform him, with Anne serving as his mentor and answering his many theological and practical questions. In the autumn, Davy started attending Avonlea School, where he shared a desk with Milty Boulter and continued his playful antics, such as making faces at Paul Irving in church. Over time, through Anne and Marilla's patience, Davy reformed significantly, winning the hearts of those around him.

label: History
value: Dora spent her earliest years under the care of Mary Keith.
unit: Dora spent her earliest years under the care of Mary Keith, whose long illness left Dora and her twin brother Davy largely without bringing up. After Mary Keith passed away, Marilla Cuthbert brought Dora and Davy to live with her at Green Gables. At Green Gables, Dora quickly gained a reputation for being an exceptionally well-behaved, quiet, and reliable child who spent her time assisting Marilla with domestic duties and maintaining immaculate clothes and garden plots. She began attending school alongside Davy and made friends, though she once got so frightened by ghost stories told by Mirabel Cotton that she cried and refused to go upstairs alone in the dark. During a fierce and destructive hailstorm at Green Gables, Dora remained calm and quiet by Anne's side throughout the ordeal.

At Green Gables, Dora quickly gained a reputation for being an exceptionally well-behaved, quiet, and reliable child who spent her time assisting Marilla with domestic duties and maintaining immaculate clothes and garden plots. She began attending school alongside Davy and made friends, though she once got so frightened by ghost stories told by Mirabel Cotton that she cried and refused to go upstairs alone in the dark. During a fierce and destructive hailstorm at Green Gables, Dora remained calm and quiet by Anne's side throughout the ordeal.

label: History
value: Gilbert lived in Alberta for three years
unit: After living in Alberta for three years with his ailing father, Gilbert returned to Avonlea and resumed his schooling, entering into an intense academic rivalry with Anne Shirley. He pursued Second Year work at Queen's Academy, successfully obtaining his First Class teacher's license in one year. Because his father could not afford to send him directly to college, Gilbert took a teaching position at White Sands. He generously surrendered his initial application for the Avonlea school to Anne so she could live at Green Gables with Marilla. In Avonlea, he was elected president of the Village Improvement Society and co-authored satirical local notes for the newspaper with Anne. After teaching for a year, he resigned his position at White Sands to prepare to attend Redmond College alongside Anne.

label: History
value: In early April, Mr. J. A. Harrison bought Robert Bell's farm in Avonlea
unit: In early April, Mr. J. A. Harrison bought Robert Bell's farm in Avonlea and moved there from New Brunswick. He initially kept house by himself without regular meal times and gained a reputation among the locals as an odd crank. After an initial confrontation with Anne Shirley over a Jersey cow, the two quickly became close friends, often spending evenings conversing on his veranda. He supported the Village Improvement Society and proved himself to be a kind, sympathetic neighbor despite his rough exterior. Later, his estranged wife Emily joined him in Avonlea after his parrot Ginger died, reuniting the couple. Following their reconciliation, Mr. Harrison began attending church every Sunday, subscribing to the minister's salary, and keeping a far neater appearance.

label: History
value: Jane went on a boat ride on the Lake of Shining Waters with her father.
unit: While out on a boat ride on the Lake of Shining Waters with her father, Jane nearly fell overboard picking water lilies but was caught by her sash in time. At school, she gamely accepted a dare from Josie Pye to hop on one leg around the garden, stopping at the third corner. She prepared a dialogue called 'A Morning Visit' with Diana Barry and Ruby Gillis for Miss Stacy's Friday afternoon recitations. Jane later attended Queen's Academy to study for her teaching license, carrying off top honors in the domestic science course. After graduating, she accepted a teaching post at Newbridge School and joined the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, where she was appointed chairman of the hall re-shingling and painting committee.

label: History
value: Josie Pye frequently engaged in dares.
unit: During her time at Avonlea school, Josie Pye frequently engaged in dares and rivalries with her classmates. On one occasion, she successfully walked a board fence after being dared by Anne Shirley, and subsequently dared Anne to walk the ridgepole of a roof, which resulted in Anne falling and breaking her ankle. During preparation for a school concert, Josie became sulky when she was not cast as the fairy queen in a dialogue because of her size. Later, she caused a three-month rift with Julia Bell after repeating a rude comment about Julia's reciting style to Bessie Wright. Josie won first prize for her knitted lace at an exhibition. She later studied for the entrance examinations and attended Queen's Academy, taking Second Class work for education's sake rather than out of necessity to earn a living.

value: Miss Lavendar is imaginative.
unit: Imaginative and fond of pretending, Miss Lavendar loves playing at tea parties and keeping up imagined worlds to compensate for her lonely life. She is exceptionally sweet, hospitable, and a good listener who charms those around her. Although she generally dislikes being kissed, she feels a special warmth and connection toward young friends who share her imaginative nature. When troubled, she can become quiet, tired, and withdrawn.

label: History
value: Lavendar lived a quiet life.
unit: Miss Lavendar lived a quiet, retired life at Echo Lodge. Ten years after her mother's death, she took in a series of young girls from the Bowman family to assist her and keep her company, calling each of them 'Charlotta' in turn. Anne Shirley and Diana Barry visited her one autumn afternoon and were immediately welcomed into her home for tea. A deep friendship grew between Anne and Miss Lavendar, bringing joy and companionship into her quiet life. Later, when Stephen Irving returned and re-entered her life, the two reconciled their past quarrel. They were married in a ceremony in her honeysuckle arbor in late August, surrounded by friends, before planning to travel and reside together in Boston.

label: History
value: Marilla Cuthbert lived at Green Gables.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert lived at Green Gables in Avonlea for sixty years alongside her brother Matthew. When they arranged to adopt an orphan boy to help on the farm, a mistake resulted in the arrival of red-haired Anne Shirley. Though initially astonished and inclined to return her, Marilla decided to keep Anne and took full charge of her upbringing. Over time, Marilla developed a deep, devoted love for Anne despite her strict discipline and struggle to manage the girl's imaginative mishaps. Following Matthew's death and experiencing failing eyesight, she continued managing Green Gables with Anne's help. She later took in her third cousins, the orphaned twins Davy and Dora Keith, providing them with a home and discipline.

label: History
value: Paul's mother passed away.
unit: After his mother passed away, Paul moved from Boston to Avonlea to live with his paternal grandmother. On his first day attending the Avonlea school, he quickly formed a deep bond of friendship with his teacher, Anne Shirley, who recognized him as a kindred spirit and a genius. Lacking local playmates near his home on the shore road, Paul invented vivid imaginary friends—such as Nora of Andrews' Cove and the Twin Sailors—with whom he shared grand adventures. At school, he proved both gentle and capable, defending his American patriotism in a drawn fight against St. Clair Donnell and later protecting younger students like Davy Keith. When Prillie Rogerson mocked his naturally curly hair, Paul dunked his head into a spring to prove it was natural, accidentally falling in completely. During a trip with Anne to Grafton, he met Miss Lavendar Lewis and immediately took a liking to her. Later, his father unexpectedly visited Avonlea, leading to a joyful reunion for Paul.

label: History
value: Mr. Phillips served as the school teacher in Avonlea.
unit: Mr. Phillips served as the school teacher in Avonlea. During his tenure, he regularly punished students, including whipping Sam Boulter—which led to an angry confrontation with Sam's father—and embarrassing Anne Shirley by holding up her slate and giving her public punishments. He paid special attention to Prissy Andrews under the guise of helping her with her lessons and openly courted her with gifts and verses. While teaching, he periodically engaged in sudden fits of strict reform, though he generally maintained poor discipline in his classroom. At an evening concert, he delivered Mark Antony's oration while gazing at Prissy. Before leaving Avonlea at the end of the term, he gave an emotional farewell speech that brought his students to tears.

value: Rachel is a capable woman.

In times of illness, she proves to be a tender, patient, and unwearied caregiver.

unit: Rachel is a capable, hardworking, and outspoken woman who prides herself on speaking her mind without fear or favor. She is an energetic community figure and a meddlesome gossip who keeps a sharp eye on everything happening around Avonlea. Despite her critical, opinionated, and nagging tendencies, she is deeply kind, well-meaning, and readily owns up when she makes a mistake. In times of illness, she proves to be a tender, patient, and unwearied caregiver.

value: Rachel Lynde lived for decades at Lynde's Hollow in Avonlea.
unit: Rachel Lynde lived for decades at Lynde's Hollow in Avonlea, actively running the local Sewing Circle and serving as a key pillar of the Church Aid Society and Foreign Missions Auxiliary. label: History
value: Ruby shared treats with Anne Shirley while attending Avonlea school.
unit: While attending Avonlea school, Ruby shared treats with Anne Shirley, participated in class events such as dialogues, and took part in a concert tableau of 'Faith, Hope and Charity'. She climbed a high willow tree on a dare from Carrie Sloane despite her fear of caterpillars. When Anne was injured playing games, Ruby panicked and succumbed to hysterics. She was accepted into the Queen's Academy class, passed the Entrance examinations halfway up the list, and studied to obtain a teaching license with the goal of teaching for two years before getting married. Upon completing Queen's, she secured a position teaching at Carmody school. There, she continued to draw numerous suitors, including Nelson Atkins and Wilbur Blair, boasting to her friends about her romantic conquests.

label: History
value: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired by the Avonlea school trustees
unit: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired by the Avonlea school trustees as the district's first lady teacher, succeeding Mr. Phillips. Upon taking charge of Avonlea school, she introduced several new routine activities, including physical culture exercises twice daily, biweekly Friday recitation sessions, and nature 'field days' in the woods to study ferns, flowers, and birds. She taught her students English poetry by heart and held a Queen's preparation class to prepare older students for the Entrance examinations. Although rumored to be leaving after her first year to accept a teaching job in her home district's grade school, she returned to Avonlea for a second year. During her tenure, she helped correct her students' grammar and advised ambitious students, such as Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe, to take up Second Year work at Queen's Academy to earn First Class teacher's licenses in a single year. At the end of June following her second year, her term and rule at Avonlea school came to an emotional close as she gave touching farewell words to her scholars.

unit: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired by the Avonlea school trustees as the district's first lady teacher, succeeding Mr. Phillips. Upon taking charge of Avonlea school, she introduced several new routine activities, including physical culture exercises twice daily, biweekly Friday recitation sessions, and nature 'field days' in the woods to study ferns, flowers, and birds. She taught her students English poetry by heart and held a Queen's preparation class to prepare older students for the Entrance examinations. Although rumored to be leaving after her first year to accept a teaching job in her home district's grade school, she returned to Avonlea for a second year.
